chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn Yazid al-Kermani, from Abu Muhammad al-Masri

He said: Abul Hasan Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) came (to Baghdad). I wrote to him asking for permission to go to Egypt to do business. He wrote back to me: 'Stay as long as God wills.' So I stayed for two years. Then in the third year I wrote to him asking for permission again. He wrote back to me: 'Go, may this be blessed for you. God will change things for you.' He said: So I left and made a lot of profit there. Chaos occurred in Baghdad and I was saved from that sedition.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abul Hasan Ar-Rida (Imam Ali ibn Musa, the 8th Shia Imam)
key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ الْمَصْرِيُّ: Abu Muhammad al-Masri (the narrator of the hadith)
key_terms.الْخُرُوجِ إِلَى مِصْرَ: Going to Egypt (a major commercial center)
key_terms.الْفِتْنَةُ: Sedition/Trial (referring to the political turmoil in Baghdad)

ai.seo_question: What was the significance of Imam Ar-Rida's advice to Abu Muhammad al-Masri regarding his travel to Egypt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Imam’s divine foresight (*‘ilm al-ghayb*) and his role as a protector of his followers during political turmoil, specifically the fitna in Baghdad. The narrative illustrates the practical wisdom of patience (*sabr*) and the spiritual authority of the Imam to alter destiny through his blessing (*baraka*), reinforcing the Shia belief in the Imam’s infallible guidance in both spiritual and worldly affairs.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 47-41 Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Waleed - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Waleed ibn Yazid al-Kermani, on the authority of Abi Muhammad al-Basri, “

Abul Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) came (to Baghdad). I asked him in writing to grant me permission to go to Egypt to do business. In response he wrote, ‘Wait to see what God wills.’ I waited for two years. In the third year I wrote to him (a.s.) and asked for permission again. He wrote back, ‘Go. May this be blessed for you. God will change things for you.’ Then I left (for Egypt) and made a lot of profit. There was chaos in Baghdad and I was saved from that sedition.”
